t: Gongsun Kang succeeds his father
c: He was succeeded by his son Gongsun Kang in 204.

t: Gongsun Kang invades Goguryeo
c: Goguryeo was invaded by warlord Gongsun Kang in 204, resulting in the Daifang Commandery.

t: Gongsun Kang invades and captures Goguryeo capital
c: In 209, Kang invaded Goguryeo again, took the capital of Goguryeo and forced them to submit.

t: Rebellion erupts in Liang Province
c: In Liang Province (present-day Gansu), rebellion had erupted in 184.

t: Cao Cao wars with Tao Qian
c: In 194, Cao Cao went to war with Tao Qian of Xu Province, because Tao's subordinate Zhang Kai had murdered Cao Cao's father Cao Song.

t: Cao Cao drives Lü Bu from Yan Province
c: A year later, in 195, Cao Cao managed to drive Lü Bu out of Yan Province.

t: Yuan Shu establishes capital at Shouchun
c: Yuan Shu, after being driven south in 193, established himself at his new capital Shouchun (present-day Anhui).

t: Yuan Shu declares himself emperor
c: In 197, Yuan Shu declared himself emperor of his own dynasty.

t: Emperor Xian comes under Cao Cao's control
c: In 196, Emperor Xian came under the protection and control of Cao Cao after he had succeeded in fleeing from the warlords of Chang'an.

t: Cao Cao raises army
c: Cao Cao, whose zone of control was the precursor to the state of Cao Wei, had raised an army in 189.

t: Dong Cheng receives edict to assassinate Cao Cao
c: In 200, Dong Cheng, an imperial relative, received a secret edict from Emperor Xian to assassinate Cao Cao.

t: Cao Cao advances after Yuan Shao's death
c: Cao Cao took advantage of Yuan Shao's death in 202, which resulted in division among his sons, and advanced to the north.

t: Cao Cao captures city of Ye
c: In 204, after the Battle of Ye, Cao Cao captured the city of Ye.

t: Huang Zu kills Sun Jian
c: In 193, Huang Zu led the forces of Liu Biao in a campaign against Sun Jian (Yuan Shu's subordinate general) and killed him.

t: Sun Ce enters Yuan Shu's service
c: In 194, Sun Ce (aged 18) came into the military service under Yuan Shu.

t: Sun Ce declares independence from Yuan Shu
c: In 198, Sun Ce (aged 23) declared his independence from Yuan Shu who recently had declared himself emperor.

t: Conquest of Yuzhang commandery and Lujiang
c: By 200, he had conquered Yuzhang commandery (at present-day Lake Poyang in Jiangxi) and Lujiang north of the Yangtze.

t: Assassination of Sun Ce
c: In 200, Sun Ce was ambushed and assassinated by the former retainers of a defeated rival from Wu.

t: Sun Quan defeats Huang Zu
c: In 208, Sun Quan defeated Huang Zu (Liu Biao's subordinate commander) around present-day Wuhan.

t: Cao Cao marches south to unify empire
c: In 208, Cao Cao marched south with his army hoping to quickly unify the empire.

t: Zhou Yu captures Jiangling
c: In 209, Zhou Yu captured Jiangling, establishing the south's complete dominance over the Yangtze River.

t: Sun Quan cedes Jiangling territory to Liu Bei
c: Sun Quan was forced to cede the territory around Jiangling to Liu Bei, because he could not establish a proper authority over it after Zhou Yu's death in 210.

t: Cao Cao defeats warlord coalition at Huayin
c: In 211, Cao Cao defeated a warlord coalition in the Wei valley, ending in the Battle of Huayin, capturing the territory around Chang'an.

t: Liu Bei accepts invitation to Yi Province
c: In 211, Liu Bei accepted an invitation from Liu Zhang to come to Yi Province for aiding the latter against a threat from the north, namely Zhang Lu of Hanzhong.

t: Cao Cao becomes Chancellor, Duke, and King of Wei
c: He became the Chancellor in 208, the Duke of Wei in 214, and the King of Wei in 217.

t: Lü Meng attempts to capture Jing commanderies
c: In 215, Lü Meng (Sun Quan's officer) was sent to capture Jing province's southern commanderies, but Guan Yu (Liu Bei's general) launched a counterattack.

t: Liu Bei seizes Hanzhong, kills Xiahou Yuan
c: In 219, Liu Bei seized Hanzhong by defeating and killing General Xiahou Yuan, who served Cao Cao.

t: Sun Quan appoints Lü Meng as successor
c: This changed when Sun Quan appointed Lü Meng when Lu Su died in 217.

t: Guan Yu sails up Han River to Fan
c: In 219, Guan Yu sailed from Jiangling up the Han River towards the city of Fan (near Xianyang), but was unable to capture it.

t: Sun Quan declares independence from Wei
c: Afterwards in 222, Sun Quan renounced his suzerainty to Wei and declared the independence of Wu.

t: Liu Shan becomes Emperor of Shu Han
c: In 223, Liu Shan rose to the throne of Shu following his father's defeat and death.

t: Zhuge Liang conquers southern territories in Yunnan
c: From 224 to 225, during his southward campaigns, Zhuge Liang conquered the southern territories up to Lake Dian in Yunnan.

t: Zhuge Liang transfers armies to Hanzhong
c: In 227, Zhuge Liang transferred his main Shu armies to Hanzhong, and opened up the battle for the northwest with Wei.

t: Zhuge Liang launches final northern offensive
c: In 234, he led his last great northern offensive, reaching the Battle of Wuzhang Plains south of the Wei River.

t: Rebellions in Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen commanderies
c: In 248, the people of Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen commanderies rebelled.

t: Cao Pi dies; Cao Rui succeeds as emperor

t: Sima Yi defends Xiangyang against Wu offensive
c: In 226, Sima Yi successfully defended Xiangyang against an offensive from Wu; this battle was the first time he had command in the field.

t: Sima Yi appointed to Chang'an military post
c: In 227, Sima Yi was appointed to a post at Chang'an where he managed the military affairs along the Han River.

t: Cao Huan becomes emperor after Cao Mao's death
c: Cao Huan succeeded to the throne in 260 after Cao Mao was killed in a failed coup against Sima Zhao.

c: After Sima Shi's death in 255, Sima Shi's younger brother Sima Zhao became the regent of Cao Wei.

t: Death of Emperor Wu of Jin
c: Emperor Wu died in 290, and Emperor Hui's ascension began the War of the Eight Princes.

t: Empress Jia seizes imperial power
c: In 291, Emperor Hui's wife, Empress Jia, seized power and began ruling the empire behind her husband's throne.

t: Huan Xuan usurps Jin throne
c: In 403, Huan Xuan, the son of esteemed general Huan Wen, usurped the Jin throne and declared the dynasty of Huan Chu.

t: Liu Yu replaces Jin emperor
c: In 419, Liu Yu had Sima Dezong strangled and replaced by his brother Sima Dewen, posthumously known as Emperor Gong.

t: Northern Wei conquers Northern Liang
c: In the north, Northern Liang, the last of the Sixteen Kingdoms, was conquered by Northern Wei in 439, ushering in the Northern dynasties period.

c: The Later Zhao was soon destroyed by Ran Min in 351.

c: In 352, his brother, Murong Ke defeated and captured Ran Min at the Battle of Liantai.

c: After Murong Jun's death in 360, Murong Ke acted as regent for his child heir and maintained the Yan's military supremacy through his competent leadership.
